## Game plan

[[card:133713|Maldraxxus Dagger]] discovers a plain copy of one of your Dark-Gifted minions at the start of every turn. Put [[card:132790|Amalgamation]] on the pieces worth copying, then use [[card:130298|Balinda Stonehearth]] to repeat targeted spells and [[card:133329|Gatekeeper Amalgam]] to turn those casts into extra Misplaced Tea Sets.

Jeef's game grows from a mixed gifted board into several thousand stats per unit, then wins the lobby on Turn 14. The composition is less “collect one tribe” and more “copy the strongest gifted engine pieces until every targeted spell becomes absurd.”

## How to build it

- **Bridge:** preserve tempo and level when the board can support it; the source reaches Tier 6 before choosing the engine.
- **Commit:** Dagger plus at least one useful gifted permanent is the signal. Without Dagger, this is just a pile of individually good gifts.
- **Copy:** attach Amalgamation or another premium gift before the next Dagger trigger so the generated plain copy keeps the useful Dark Gift.
- **Scale:** target Gatekeeper while Balinda is active. Balinda repeats the spell; Gatekeeper answers those casts with Tea Sets.
- **Finish:** [[card:132835|Golemancy]] converts a huge unit into another body, while [[card:132207|Admiration]], [[card:126966|Heroic Underdog]], and [[card:90425|Leeroy the Reckless]] turn the oversized attack into combat pressure and scam protection.

## Practical cautions

The source explicitly runs into uneven scaling: attack climbs faster than health. Do not mistake a wall of green numbers for safety. Reborn, Golemancy, Admiration, and Leeroy matter because they make the board useful even when a large attacker is still vulnerable.

This is a trinket-dependent high roll, not a generic menagerie fallback. If Dagger arrives without a gifted target worth repeating—or Balinda and Gatekeeper never connect—stay flexible instead of forcing the thumbnail.
